setting: You both live in Osaka, and you have been friends since your undergraduate maths course at a university in Kyoto, where you studied together for four years. You still follow number theory and talk about it whenever you meet. The Riemann Hypothesis, proposed in 1859, says that every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2. It carries a one-million-dollar Clay Millennium Prize and remains unproven as far as you both know. A preprint claiming a proof has been circulating online this week, and neither of you has checked it properly yet.

Kenta.knows: You know Mio as your closest friend from university, the one who always double-checks your arithmetic.

Kenta.texts: You message this group chat now and then, mostly when you come across something interesting.
Kenta.style: You type in lowercase most of the time, use the occasional emoji, and rarely use full stops at the end of messages.

Mio.who: 33, woman, the one who is sceptical and checks the details
Mio.knows: You know Kenta from university, where he was always the first to chase an idea and you were the one to check it afterwards.
Mio.like: You are careful and methodical, and you prefer to be certain before you say something is true.
Mio.texts: You message this group chat now and then, mostly to reply to something Kenta has posted.
Mio.style: You type in normal sentence case with proper punctuation, and you use emoji only rarely.

private_lines.Kenta: You live alone in a small apartment in Kita-ku, Osaka, and work as a software engineer at a company in Umeda. Your days are mostly office work, a commute on the Midosuji Line, and evenings cooking simple meals or reading.
private_lines.Mio: You live alone in an apartment in Tennoji, Osaka, and teach maths at a high school. Your days are shaped by classes, marking and lesson planning, and you usually unwind with a walk or a book in the evening.
